inputs.statement: V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generators x,y,h of sl₂(ℂ) act on V and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.

The natural tensor maps give K-linear isomorphisms V_K≅M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K, intertwining all lattice operators. There exists a K-basis (b_i)_{i∈I} of V_K obtained from an R-basis (b e_i) of M_R with b∈J nonzero. In particular dim_K(V_K)=n=λ+1>0. On this basis the induced operators satisfy xb_0=0, xb_i=(λ−i+1)b_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, yb_i=(i+1)b_(i+1) for i<λ, yb_λ=0, hb_i=(λ−2i)b_i, with integer coefficients interpreted in K. For every 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K and the induced divided powers X_r,Y_r equal (r!)^(-1)x^r,(r!)^(-1)y^r. Every binom(λ,j) for j∈I is nonzero in K. The reduced operators T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ−i)(Y_λ X_λ)Y_(λ−j), for i,j∈I, obey T_ij b_k=δ_jk b_i for every k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 for j=k and 0 otherwise.

inputs.statement: p is a prime number and K has characteristic p.

output.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

argument.text: Choose the basis beta supplied by N005 and define T by its displayed formula. Let W⊆V_K be any K-linear subspace. Assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. Closure under x,y implies closure under their nonnegative powers. The divided-power indices in T_ij are λ−i,λ,λ−j, all within 0,…,λ; N005 identifies the corresponding X,Y with scalar multiples of those powers. A linear subspace is closed under scalar multiplication and compositions of preserving maps, so W is invariant under every T_ij.
In the zero case temporarily assume L2: W={0}. Then the desired disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately. Discharge L2 to obtain the implication for this case.

produces.statement: If W={0}, then W={0} or W=V_K.

argument.text: For the other case assume L3: W≠{0}. A nonzero subspace contains a nonzero vector, and the beta basis of N005 expands any such vector uniquely. Its coefficients cannot all be zero. Thus there exist a vector w∈W, a coefficient family c∈K^I and an index j∈I with w=∑_{k∈I}c_k beta_k, w≠0 and c_j≠0. Record this compatible joint existence before choosing the witnesses.

produces.statement: There exist w0∈W, c0∈K^I and j0∈I such that w0≠0, w0=∑_{k∈I}c0_k beta_k, and c0_j0≠0.

argument.text: Choose compatible w,c,j as in F003. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit action of N005 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. By F001 this vector belongs to W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives beta_i∈W. This holds for every i; since beta is a K-basis, W=V_K. No chosen vector or coordinate is present in that conclusion. Discharge L3 to obtain: if W≠{0}, then W=V_K.

Classical case elimination on W={0} or W≠{0}, using F002 and F004, gives W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W: every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V_K. N005 also gives dim_K V_K=λ+1>0, so V_K is nonzero. By H003 and the definition of L_K, x,y,h span its lattice-induced action; invariance under those generators is equivalent to L_K-invariance. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.
